daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo convened business leaders from Kadin at the State Palace, where he signaled his support for Destry as a candidate for BI Governor. Kadin announced four quick-win programs to support the government, and reaffirmed its backing for Prabowo's 8 percent economic growth target. The presidential office confirmed that 8,100 tickets will be opened for the 81st Independence Day ceremony at the palace, and that Prabowo will lead the ceremony in Jakarta.

  • The Constitutional Court's ruling on the free meal program (MBG) budget prompted the presidential palace to state it would respect and study the decision, while observers warned the program could lose up to Rp 220 trillion in funding.
  • The Istana firmly denied any cabinet reshuffle plans in early August, and responded to declining poll numbers for Prabowo from SMRC.
  • A parliamentary watchdog report card showed the DPR's oversight and integrity functions received a D grade for 2025.
  • The Badan Gizi Nasional (BGN) announced it will submit a budget scheme for MBG to the Finance Ministry following the MK ruling.
  • Head of BGN Sudaryono addressed reports that a BGN employee was transferred to Papua for using a phone during a meeting.
  • Regional governments warned they cannot afford to pay employee salaries after transfer cuts (TKD), with one official planning to meet Prabowo on the issue.
  • President Prabowo announced a cleanest city competition with Rp 20 billion in prizes.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo disclosed that South Korea has requested him to open talks with North Korea, and confirmed he is prepared to travel to North Korea. Speaking at a separate event, the president urged calm as global tensions rise.

  • Indonesia and Norway deepened their climate partnership with a US$216 million fund.
  • Indonesia and Australia strengthened disaster management collaboration.
  • Indonesia and Malaysia are coordinating on a pilot drug smuggling case.
  • The U.S. Ambassador to ASEAN stated that the U.S. respects ASEAN's handling of South China Sea issues.
  • Japan reaffirmed support for ASEAN centrality amid geopolitical tensions.

Other

Pertamina lowered Pertamax fuel prices effective 1 August. The government is advancing multiple social and economic programs, including targeting high-stunting regions for the free meal initiative and working to improve fishermen welfare by 2027. The national village cooperative program reported that 33,758 participants have graduated as managers, though gender imbalances persist and salary details remain unclear, despite Rp 1 trillion spent on training.

  • The state printing company PERURI launched a Merah Putih chip design sandbox to advance digital sovereignty.
  • The Directorate General of Intellectual Property announced that music copyright registration will be free starting 1 August.
  • Indonesia is addressing 294 drought hotspots to protect food security, while the environment ministry expanded the national nursery network to boost seedling supply.
  • The home affairs minister is pushing e-Government integration to improve social aid distribution accuracy.
  • The health ministry announced that heart screening will be expanded to lower mortality rates, and that hospital accreditation will focus on patient safety.
